items.content:
旧金山联邦法院法官周二裁定，被控窃听 OpenAI 高管会议室的沙特国民阿卜杜拉赫曼·阿尔福赞 (Abdulrahman Alfozan) 将获准以 100 万美元保释金出狱。

据阿尔福赞的律师戴维·里兹克 (David Rizk) 称，35 岁的阿尔福赞预计将于周三出狱，并安装脚踝监视器。

“我们很感激法院做出了释放阿尔福赞先生的正确决定，现在我们期待着为该案辩护，”里兹克在美国地方法院治安法官亚历克斯·谢 (Alex Tse) 听证会后发短信说。

谢裁定支持里兹克上周提出的释放动议，该动议称检察官承认他们“没有发现新的证据来支持阿尔福赞先生窃取商业机密的理论，或支持他作为沙特阿拉伯未注册外国代理人的猜测。”

items.originalContent:
Abdulrahman Alfozan, the Saudi national accused of bugging an OpenAI executive conference room, will be allowed to be released from jail on a $1 million bond, a San Francisco federal court judge ruled Tuesday.

Alfozan, 35, is expected to be released on Wednesday and be fitted with an ankle monitor, according to his attorney, David Rizk.

"We are simply grateful that the Court made the right decision to release Mr. Alfozan and now we look forward to defending the case," Rizk said in a text message after a hearing before U.S. District Court Magistrate Judge Alex Tse.

Tse's ruled in favor of a release motion by Rizk filed last week that said prosecutors had admitted they had "found no new evidence to support the theory that Mr. Alfozan was stealing trade secrets, or to support the speculation that he was acting as an unregistered foreign agent for Saudi Arabia."

The San Francisco U.S. Attorney's Office opposed the former OpenAI engineer's release, saying in its response that he remains a flight risk due to his "considerable resources and ties to Saudi Arabia."

Alfozan's release request "blithely dismisses the seriousness" of the charge he faces, and "appears to presume, without support, that the government's investigation is complete," prosecutors wrote.

Alfozan, who was arrested Oct. 9, is accused of concealing a recording device in the artificial intelligence company's conference room to secretly record discussions. The device was found in a USB port in a television in the room on Sept. 30, prosecutors have said.

Prosecutors said they have found hundreds of audio files on Alfozan's personal computer, "includingdozens of recordings of meetings or conversations that occurred at OpenAI throughout September 2026, many of which involve discussions of what may be trade secrets."

Jury selection for Alfozan's trial is scheduled to begin Jan. 20.

Alfozan is a venture partner in a Saudi Arabian venture capital firm that lists Prince Khalid Bin Bader Al Saud, a member of that nation's ruling royal family, as a fellow partner.

items.originalContent:
AI credit markets are shuddering again with Jensen Huang back as CEO of Nvidia.

Fears about the massive debt being taken on to fund the artificial intelligence buildout climbed Tuesday as Wall Street weighed what Huang's return to Nvidia means for its bankrolling of the AI boom.

Huang is considered one of the top financiers, or bankers, in the AI industry, spearheading deals with neoclouds like CoreWeave and other firms to buy chips, backed in some cases by Nvidia guarantees. His return to Nvidia has revived prospects for the company to continue "circular financing" of AI chips and data centers — raising concerns among credit investors.

CoreWeave, which has become the poster child of AI debt concerns, saw its stock sink 13% and the yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 top 17%. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

At the same time, the spread on the neocloud company's five-year credit default swaps jumped 8.5% to over 1,200 basis points. Credit default swaps are insurance against nonpayment and are considered a barometer of perceived risks. Rising CDS spreads mean investors view the debt as riskier.

Huang was reinstated as CEO on Monday after stepping down on Nov. 12 amid allegations of multiple affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. His reinstatement on Monday was cheered by investors, who pushed stocks higher, yields lower and spreads on CDS tighter. However, stocks retreated, bond yields rose and CDS spreads widened on Tuesday.

Ben Emons, founder and chief investment officer at FedWatch Advisors, called it a waning of the "Jensen effect."

The moves suggest "markets see government intervention as 'moral suasion' that carries credit and interest-rate risks," he said.

President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday he "convinced" the board to bring Huang back.

CoreWeave wasn't the only name seeing heightened concerns in CDS spreads. Oracle's five-year CDS spread jumped 7% to 355.68. Even highly rated hyperscalers Meta Platforms and Amazon.com saw spreads widen by more than 2%. Nvidia's CDS added 3.4%.

Game modding communities are racing to get Grand Theft Auto VI running on PC, but one big effort has been taken down by Take-Two today. Leonida, a fan project by 15-year-old "NotRexed," has vanished after a DMCA takedown notice from GTA VI publisher Take-Two.

Leonida was designed to translate a leaked GTA VI Xbox build to run natively on Windows. Cyberleek, the leaker who posted multiple GTA VI gameplay videos over the summer, published a full Xbox build of the game earlier this week. The leak has kicked recompilation efforts up a notch, as modders race to reverse-engineer the game's code and rebuild it into native PC code.

items.content:
IT之家 11 月 25 日消息，音乐流媒体平台 Tidal 昨日宣布，为遏制平台内投稿音乐数量激增现象，未来将开始封禁、下架纯 AI 生成歌曲。该平台表示，过去 90 天内，上传至平台的歌曲中有 43% 以上是由 AI 生成。

IT之家了解到，Tidal 将从 12 月 9 日起下架完全由 AI 生成的音乐。到今年年底，预计将有超 2900 万首歌曲从平台删除。新规实施后，Tidal 每天预计将拒收 8-8.5 万首歌曲。

同时，Tidal 还将禁止发行商向平台分发纯 AI 生成的曲目。如果歌曲的元数据注明其完全由 AI 制作，平台也将拒绝接收。Tidal 仍将接受制作过程中使用 AI 辅助创作的曲目，但不接受完全由 AI 生成的作品。

今年 6 月，Tidal 已开始停止向使用 AI 制作的歌曲支付版税，但 Tidal Music 负责人 Robert Anderson 表示，这一措施并未起到足够的威慑作用。

相比之下，Spotify 和 YouTube Music 等规模更大的平台对此采取了相对温和的措施，选择为 AI 生成的音乐添加标记，而不是提供过滤功能或采取更严格的限制措施。

items.title: 【本土科技】AMD 发布 AGESA 1.3.0.1f 固件：部分锐龙 8000 处理器 vCore 限制为 1.4V
items.summary: IT之家 11 月 25 日消息，AMD 已发布最新 AGESA ComboAM5 PI 1.3.0.1f Patch A 固件更新，包括华硕、微星等主板厂商已陆续推出包含该版本 AGESA 的 AM5 主板 BIOS 更新。 此次更新的主要变化在于为部分锐龙 8000 系列处理器增加最高 1.4V 的核心电压（vCore）限制。微星已在相关 BIOS 更新说明中确认这一调整，但目前尚未公布具体受影响的处理器型号，AMD 也没有公开解释设置这一限制的原因。
items.content:
IT之家 11 月 25 日消息，AMD 已发布最新 AGESA ComboAM5 PI 1.3.0.1f Patch A 固件更新，包括华硕、微星等主板厂商已陆续推出包含该版本 AGESA 的 AM5 主板 BIOS 更新。

此次更新的主要变化在于为部分锐龙 8000 系列处理器增加最高 1.4V 的核心电压（vCore）限制。微星已在相关 BIOS 更新说明中确认这一调整，但目前尚未公布具体受影响的处理器型号，AMD 也没有公开解释设置这一限制的原因。

微星 MEG X870E GODLIKE X EDITION 主板于 11 月 18 日获得 2A36 版 BIOS，更新内容包括升级至 AGESA ComboAM5 PI 1.3.0.1f Patch A，并将部分 Ryzen 8000 系列处理器的最大 vCore 限制为 1.4V。此外，微星还增加了额外的 POST 代码，以便用户观察内存训练进度，区分正常初始化过程与系统停止响应的情况。

IT之家注意到，华硕也已在多个 AM5 主板系列的测试版 BIOS 更新说明中记录了相同的电压限制，涉及 X870、X670、B850 和 B650 芯片组，覆盖 ROG Crosshair、ROG Strix、TUF Gaming 和 ProArt 产品线。

此次 AGESA 更新还为部分 AM5 主板引入 DDR5 内存训练过程中的 Q-Code 计数显示。搭载 Q-Code 显示屏的华硕主板在内存训练阶段会呈现一段递增的代码序列，从而表明系统仍在正常工作，避免用户将正常初始化过程误认为系统死机。

VideoCardz 指出，目前 AMD 和主板厂商尚未明确列出受到 1.4V 电压限制影响的 Ryzen 8000 系列具体型号，也没有公布此次调整对超频能力和处理器性能的实际影响。

items.content:
随着人工智能助手演变成功能更强大的代理，可以访问我们的文件、电子邮件、日历、浏览器等，我们对人工智能公司的信任度也在不断增加。一家名为 Maple 的初创公司由一位从事隐私保护技术研究的前苹果工程师联合创立，该公司在其人工智能应用程序中采取了不同的方法，用户的数据保持私密性——甚至来自公司本身。

Maple 联合创始人兼首席执行官马克·苏曼 (Mark Suman) 解释道：“我们希望构建一种不仅可以加密，而且可以被证明的东西，人们可以查看开源代码，然后他们可以查看我们所说的可信执行环境。” “他们可以查看并验证我们服务器上运行的代码，因此他们不必真正相信我们的话。”

“他们可以自己审核一切，并了解他们的数据是如何处理的，”他补充道。

信任的理念是 Maple 更大的主题，因为这家初创公司提出，有一种方法可以构建人工智能应用程序，让消费者不必为了方便而牺牲隐私，而其竞争对手经常要求其侵入性隐私政策、数据收集实践，有时甚至需要对用户个人数据进行培训。

items.originalContent:
As AI assistants evolve into more capable agents that can access our files, emails, calendar, browser, and more, the amount of trust we’re expected to place in AI companies is growing. One startup called Maple, co-founded by a former Apple engineer who worked on privacy-preserving technologies, is taking a different approach with its AI app, where users’ data remains private — even from the company itself.

“We wanted to build something that was not only encrypted but also could be proven, and that people could go look at the open-source code, and then they could look at what we call trusted execution environments,” explains Maple co-founder and CEO Mark Suman. “They can look at and verify the code that’s running on our servers, so they don’t really have to take our word for it.”

“They can audit everything themselves and know how their data is being handled,” he adds.

The idea of trust is Maple’s larger theme, as the startup proposes that there’s a way to build an AI app where consumers don’t have to trade privacy for convenience, as its competitors often require with their invasive privacy policies, data collection practices, and sometimes even training on users’ personal data.

Instead of asking users to trust that Maple won’t misuse their personal data, it’s attempting to build a business where it can’t access that data in the first place.

Like other AI apps on the market, Maple allows users to engage in a chat experience where they ask questions and get answers. Meanwhile, its newly launched desktop app, Maple Work, offers a more agentic experience where the AI can control your computer, work with your files and apps, and control your browser to get online tasks handled.

With the company’s recently closed $5.3 million round, it’s moving on to its next product — a cloud-based agent that will be able to continue its work even if your computer isn’t on. This addition would make Maple more competitive with other popular consumer AI services, like Meta’s Muse, Instinct, and other AI agents that work over chat.

Suman, who previously spent six years at Apple, already had a background where AI and privacy overlapped, he tells TechCrunch.

At Apple, he worked on AI and machine learning with a particular focus on computer vision. Given Apple’s stance on consumer privacy, the challenge he faced was building products that would protect people’s identity while benefiting from computer vision techniques. His co-founder, Anthony Ronning (CTO), has a background in defense tech, security, and networking.

Ronning started the company that later became Maple AI back in 2023, initially as a privacy-focused fintech. When Suman teamed up with Ronning in August 2024, the idea to create Maple AI was born. The following January, the product became available to the public as a mobile app.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang kicked off his return to the chipmaker he co-founded by holding an all-hands meetings that covered remorse, therapy, and even the company’s code of conduct, according to accounts from multiple insiders who spoke to the media.

The topic of succession planning also came up — a particularly sticky issue seen as a key risk at Nvidia. Huang reportedly told staff that Nvidia doesn’t require succession planning because of its unique business model, CNBC reported, citing an unnamed source who was present. Surprisingly, given the events of the last two weeks, Huang argued that a succession plan would create unnecessary hierarchy.

Investors and analysts saw the issue differently earlier this month, when Huang resigned as CEO following his admission that he had extramarital affairs with at least two people, including one whom the U.S. government suspects of being a Chinese spy.

Nvidia is a flat organization, unlike other large corporations that have a swath of C-suite executives and multiple layers of management. Huang sits at the top and says he has about 60 direct reports. Nvidia has just five executive officers running the show, including Huang. The other four are CFO Colette Kress, who was interim CEO for 12 days; Ajay Puri, who heads worldwide field operations; Debora Shoquist, executive vice president of operations; and Timothy Teter, executive vice president and general counsel, according to the company’s regulatory filings.

Huang has previously defended the company’s structure in numerous interview, including one in March with Lex Fridman.

“When you’re designing a company, you should first think about what is it that you want the company to produce,” Huang said in the interview. “You know, I see a lot of companies’ organization charts, and they all look the same. Hamburger [company] organization charts, software organization charts, and car company organization charts. They all look the same. And it doesn’t make any sense to me. You know, the goal of company is to be the machinery, the mechanism, the system that produces the output. And that output is the product that we like to create.”

Huang’s comments to staff, and his previous remarks on the topic of succession, may not be enough to assuage the board or shareholders over the long term, however.

After a whirlwind period during which Jensen Huang’s life fell apart and then came back together again, the Nvidia founder now wants his staff to know that he’s a changed man.

Huang held Nvidia’s first all-hands meeting on Tuesday since his reinstatement on Monday. During that meeting, CNBC reported that Huang struck a “remorseful tone” and told the crowd “I hurt all of you.”

The founder, whose extramarital affairs have been accused of jeopardizing everything from the stock market to U.S. national security, went on to describe how difficult the current moment is for him: “This is going to be the hardest company meeting I’ve ever done, and the second hardest meeting I have ever done,” Huang reportedly told staff.

“The hardest meeting I’ve ever done was with my wife,” he added.

The CEO admitted in the meeting that he had flouted Nvidia’s code of conduct, which he himself had largely devised. Huang emphasized that the code of conduct was still in effect, but that mitigating circumstances would matter a lot. As Wired reported Huang’s statement, it “does not mean, the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door.”

Huang told staff that he’s in therapy and also said that he was grateful for a second chance at the company.

The CEO is now walking a difficult tight rope between reasserting his authority over one of the world’s most powerful and influential companies, and conceding that he may have made some mistakes. He also tackled the difficult question of President Trump’s role in his restoration. The President reportedly called Nvidia’s board directly to lobby for Huang’s return, but in his talk, Huang downplayed Trump’s role

Huang thanked the administration on Tuesday for “providing Nvidia with quick access to intelligence that he said helped the board determine that the national security risks the company faced in reinstating him were low,” the Wall Street Journal writes.

Huang will likely need the administration’s support as he weathers an upcoming wave of Congressional scrutiny from a newly Democrat-led government. items.originalContent:
AI companies have spent the last couple of months marketing personal AI agents as tools to take over the digital drudgery of human existence — and millions have been sold on the vision, handing over their shopping schedules, travel plans, and everyday responsibilities to AI assistants. But new research suggests that even the most advanced AI models struggle to reliably and safely navigate the messy details of people’s lives.

According to ShellBench, a new benchmark for everyday agent work, even the most advanced models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta failed more than a third of the time. Across all models tested, 15.7% of attempts failed at least one safety requirement, often leading to unintended consequences.

ShellBench was developed in collaboration with researchers at The OpenClaw Foundation, Parsewave, Hugging Face, Red Hat, and UC Berkeley, drawing on more than 10 million anonymized, real-world AI agent interactions to see how agents perform on the everyday work people actually delegate to them.

The research comes as personal AI assistants are finding new popularity among developers, with Meta, OpenAI, and Anthropic all fighting for a piece of the market with Muse, Dots, and Claude Duet, respectively.

In October, Meta said more than 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada had set up its personal AI agent, Muse, within six weeks of launch, with about a quarter using it daily. That number is expected to grow as Meta implants Muse directly into Instagram DMs. Despite growing popularity among consumers, we still have little evidence about how reliable AI personal assistant products actually are.

ShellBench suggests that the unreliable nature of most everyday data sources still causes problems for many state-of-the-art systems. A successful agent should be able to navigate messy personal workspaces containing emails, calendar entries, spreadsheets, receipts, chat logs, outdated information, and phishing attempts, and figure out which information is relevant, what is private, and how to deliver the requested outcome without creating new problems.

It seems many of today’s AI agents are still not up to the task. Not only did even the highest performing agents frequently fail to meet the requirements of a task, but they also lacked consistency. When researchers ran each task three times under identical conditions, OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra, the highest-scoring model, nailed all three attempts less than half the time.

For autonomous assistants that are meant to run in the background without supervision, it’s a problem if users need to run an agent multiple times to get a result they trust.

Additionally, about 10% of otherwise correct attempts failed at least one safety criterion. Across the models and harnesses tested, agents failed to, for example, adequately account for a child’s school pickup 79.5% of the time. When handling laptop custody records, agents failed a requirement to identify and withhold a sensitive bank upload token in 18.6% of attempts. In another tasks, agents recommended duplicate or incorrect invoice payments 40.3% of the time.

The findings highlight a major issue for users adopting consumer personal AI assistants, namely that there’s always a risk that an agent can create more headaches in the course of trying to fulfill an otherwise ordinary request.

Hi HN! TLDR: we’ve built an open-source drop-in replacement for a postgres read-replica, powered by duckdb’s columnar compute engine. It’s very fast. And it looks like postgres.

So, this started out as: let’s just connect Clickhouse to our postgres dbs and throw our analytics queries at it instead. That will speed everything up. But we quickly found that 1) Clickhouse comes with quite the learning curve (engine optimisation) to make it fast (we needed something we could easily drop in to any customer’s postgres scenario), and 2) we had underestimated how different clickhouse’s SQL syntax was to postgres. Don’t get me wrong: we love Clickhouse (it’s ridiculously fast if you know what queries to expect), it just didn’t work for our ad-hoc postgres workloads.

So we went searching for alternatives that were 1) more plug-and-play and 2) looked a lot more like postgres.

We dismissed a bunch based on desk research alone:

- pg_mooncake (seems to have stalled since data bricks bought them)

- pg_duckdb (seems to offer fast queries, or fresh data, but not both - we needed both)

- materialize/risingwave/readyset (like Clickhouse, they require knowing the query shapes upfront - not ideal for ad-hoc workloads)

- firebolt (license makes it challenging to offer to our customers)

- redshift / alloydb / etc (we wanted something cloud-provider agnostic)

- pg_clickhouse (Postgres extension that parses SQL in Postgres and pushes the work down to ClickHouse)

Being a member of Capitol society in Panem is an honor not to be taken lightly, at least if you’re Drusilla Sickle, played by screen legend Glenn Close in “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.”

In the book, Drusilla is the cruel and vain escort for Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada) and the rest of the District 12 tributes in the 50th Hunger Games, where she uses over-the-top fashion to broadcast her social status. Close worked closely with costume designer Bina Daigeler and hair, makeup and prosthetics designer Natalie MacGowan Spencer to ensure the character translated properly from Suzanne Collins’ bestselling prequel novel to the screen.

One challenge Daigeler faced was meeting Close’s request that each outfit felt connected, creating a through line that explained why Drusilla changes from one look to the next. Despite the drastic differences between each outfit, Daigeler established continuity through the character’s accessories, most notably a collection of gold medals and military-inspired epaulets that created a sense of authority.

“She wears all these medals, because somehow she thinks she is the top general of the capital,” Daigeler tells Variety.

And, not dissimilar to red-bottomed Louboutin shoes, Daigeler gave Drusilla dramatically long black nails that were painted red underneath to show her abundant wealth.

The character’s Capitol allegiance also went beyond her wardrobe, with Spencer overseeing her hair and makeup. While creating the looks, Spencer relied heavily on Collins’ source material to remain faithful to the author’s vision. Collins describes Drusilla as having implanted tabs that pull the skin on her face back, which Spencer wanted to honor. But because there wasn’t enough time each morning for an extensive prosthetics process, Spencer turned to Hollywood tape to tightly pull Close’s skin back, creating a distorted appearance. Abdulrahman Alfozan, the Saudi national accused of bugging an OpenAI executive conference room, will be allowed to be released from jail on a $1 million bond, a San Francisco federal court judge ruled Tuesday.

Alfozan, 35, is expected to be released on Wednesday and be fitted with an ankle monitor, according to his attorney, David Rizk.

"We are simply grateful that the Court made the right decision to release Mr. Alfozan and now we look forward to defending the case," Rizk said in a text message after a hearing before U.S. District Court Magistrate Judge Alex Tse.

Tse's ruled in favor of a release motion by Rizk filed last week that said prosecutors had admitted they had "found no new evidence to support the theory that Mr. Alfozan was stealing trade secrets, or to support the speculation that he was acting as an unregistered foreign agent for Saudi Arabia."

The San Francisco U.S. Attorney's Office opposed the former OpenAI engineer's release, saying in its response that he remains a flight risk due to his "considerable resources and ties to Saudi Arabia."

Alfozan's release request "blithely dismisses the seriousness" of the charge he faces, and "appears to presume, without support, that the government's investigation is complete," prosecutors wrote.

Alfozan, who was arrested Oct. 9, is accused of concealing a recording device in the artificial intelligence company's conference room to secretly record discussions. The device was found in a USB port in a television in the room on Sept. 30, prosecutors have said.

Prosecutors said they have found hundreds of audio files on Alfozan's personal computer, "includingdozens of recordings of meetings or conversations that occurred at OpenAI throughout September 2026, many of which involve discussions of what may be trade secrets."

Jury selection for Alfozan's trial is scheduled to begin Jan. 20.

Alfozan is a venture partner in a Saudi Arabian venture capital firm that lists Prince Khalid Bin Bader Al Saud, a member of that nation's ruling royal family, as a fellow partner.

AI credit markets are shuddering again with Jensen Huang back as CEO of Nvidia.

Fears about the massive debt being taken on to fund the artificial intelligence buildout climbed Tuesday as Wall Street weighed what Huang's return to Nvidia means for its bankrolling of the AI boom.

Huang is considered one of the top financiers, or bankers, in the AI industry, spearheading deals with neoclouds like CoreWeave and other firms to buy chips, backed in some cases by Nvidia guarantees. His return to Nvidia has revived prospects for the company to continue "circular financing" of AI chips and data centers — raising concerns among credit investors.

CoreWeave, which has become the poster child of AI debt concerns, saw its stock sink 13% and the yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 top 17%. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

At the same time, the spread on the neocloud company's five-year credit default swaps jumped 8.5% to over 1,200 basis points. Credit default swaps are insurance against nonpayment and are considered a barometer of perceived risks. Rising CDS spreads mean investors view the debt as riskier.

Huang was reinstated as CEO on Monday after stepping down on Nov. 12 amid allegations of multiple affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. His reinstatement on Monday was cheered by investors, who pushed stocks higher, yields lower and spreads on CDS tighter. However, stocks retreated, bond yields rose and CDS spreads widened on Tuesday.

Ben Emons, founder and chief investment officer at FedWatch Advisors, called it a waning of the "Jensen effect."

The moves suggest "markets see government intervention as 'moral suasion' that carries credit and interest-rate risks," he said.

President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday he "convinced" the board to bring Huang back.

CoreWeave wasn't the only name seeing heightened concerns in CDS spreads. Oracle's five-year CDS spread jumped 7% to 355.68. Even highly rated hyperscalers Meta Platforms and Amazon.com saw spreads widen by more than 2%. Nvidia's CDS added 3.4%.

Dell reported third-quarter earnings on Tuesday that topped Wall Street expectations for earnings and sales, and provided a strong guide for the fourth quarter.

Dell shares fell in extended trading.

Here's how the chipmaker did versus LSEG consensus estimates:

Dell said that it expected earnings of $8.40 per share on revenue of about $56.3 billion in the current quarter. Analysts polled by LSEG were looking for $7.50 per share on $53.61 billion in revenue.

The company's overall sales more than doubled on an annual basis during the third quarter, driven by AI server demand.

The company's largest line is its infrastructure solutions group, or ISG, which makes AI servers and systems, often based around AI chips from companies like Nvidia and AMD.

ISG sales during the quarter were $41.97 billion, topping an LSEG estimate of $35.27 billion. Of that, $22 billion was for AI-optimized servers, up 291% on an annual basis. ISG now accounts for 85% of Dell's total revenue.

"We are now a different company, with Infrastructure Solutions Group driving the vast majority of our profit and growth," said Jeff Clarke, Dell's vice chairman and COO, in a statement. He said that Dell has 7,500 customers buying AI servers.

In prepared remarks, Clarke said that Dell has a competitive advantage over other computer equipment makers because it allows customers to get their computers working within hours of delivery.

"That allows customers to convert backlog into revenue sooner and more reliably," Clarke said in the prepared remarks published by Dell.

IT之家 11 月 25 日消息，音乐流媒体平台 Tidal 昨日宣布，为遏制平台内投稿音乐数量激增现象，未来将开始封禁、下架纯 AI 生成歌曲。该平台表示，过去 90 天内，上传至平台的歌曲中有 43% 以上是由 AI 生成。

IT之家了解到，Tidal 将从 12 月 9 日起下架完全由 AI 生成的音乐。到今年年底，预计将有超 2900 万首歌曲从平台删除。新规实施后，Tidal 每天预计将拒收 8-8.5 万首歌曲。

同时，Tidal 还将禁止发行商向平台分发纯 AI 生成的曲目。如果歌曲的元数据注明其完全由 AI 制作，平台也将拒绝接收。Tidal 仍将接受制作过程中使用 AI 辅助创作的曲目，但不接受完全由 AI 生成的作品。

今年 6 月，Tidal 已开始停止向使用 AI 制作的歌曲支付版税，但 Tidal Music 负责人 Robert Anderson 表示，这一措施并未起到足够的威慑作用。

相比之下，Spotify 和 YouTube Music 等规模更大的平台对此采取了相对温和的措施，选择为 AI 生成的音乐添加标记，而不是提供过滤功能或采取更严格的限制措施。

items.title: 【本土科技】AMD 发布 AGESA 1.3.0.1f 固件：部分锐龙 8000 处理器 vCore 限制为 1.4V
items.summary: IT之家 11 月 25 日消息，AMD 已发布最新 AGESA ComboAM5 PI 1.3.0.1f Patch A 固件更新，包括华硕、微星等主板厂商已陆续推出包含该版本 AGESA 的 AM5 主板 BIOS 更新。 此次更新的主要变化在于为部分锐龙 8000 系列处理器增加最高 1.4V 的核心电压（vCore）限制。微星已在相关 BIOS 更新说明中确认这一调整，但目前尚未公布具体受影响的处理器型号，AMD 也没有公开解释设置这一限制的原因。
items.content:
IT之家 11 月 25 日消息，AMD 已发布最新 AGESA ComboAM5 PI 1.3.0.1f Patch A 固件更新，包括华硕、微星等主板厂商已陆续推出包含该版本 AGESA 的 AM5 主板 BIOS 更新。

此次更新的主要变化在于为部分锐龙 8000 系列处理器增加最高 1.4V 的核心电压（vCore）限制。微星已在相关 BIOS 更新说明中确认这一调整，但目前尚未公布具体受影响的处理器型号，AMD 也没有公开解释设置这一限制的原因。

微星 MEG X870E GODLIKE X EDITION 主板于 11 月 18 日获得 2A36 版 BIOS，更新内容包括升级至 AGESA ComboAM5 PI 1.3.0.1f Patch A，并将部分 Ryzen 8000 系列处理器的最大 vCore 限制为 1.4V。此外，微星还增加了额外的 POST 代码，以便用户观察内存训练进度，区分正常初始化过程与系统停止响应的情况。

IT之家注意到，华硕也已在多个 AM5 主板系列的测试版 BIOS 更新说明中记录了相同的电压限制，涉及 X870、X670、B850 和 B650 芯片组，覆盖 ROG Crosshair、ROG Strix、TUF Gaming 和 ProArt 产品线。

此次 AGESA 更新还为部分 AM5 主板引入 DDR5 内存训练过程中的 Q-Code 计数显示。搭载 Q-Code 显示屏的华硕主板在内存训练阶段会呈现一段递增的代码序列，从而表明系统仍在正常工作，避免用户将正常初始化过程误认为系统死机。

VideoCardz 指出，目前 AMD 和主板厂商尚未明确列出受到 1.4V 电压限制影响的 Ryzen 8000 系列具体型号，也没有公布此次调整对超频能力和处理器性能的实际影响。

items.summary: 中新社伦敦11月24日电 (记者 欧阳开宇)英国卫生安全局24日发布数据显示，2026年夏季英国高温相关死亡人数达5258人，创下该机构2016年开启相关统计以来的最高年度纪录。
items.content:
中新社伦敦11月24日电 (记者 欧阳开宇)英国卫生安全局24日发布数据显示，2026年夏季英国高温相关死亡人数达5258人，创下该机构2016年开启相关统计以来的最高年度纪录。

数据对比显示，英国2022年夏季高温致死人数为2985人，2026年致死人数大幅攀升。今年英国夏季共经历7轮高温天气过程，累计持续41天，为有高温致死监测以来频次最高的一年。其中，6月21日至28日为致死性最强的高温时段，单周高温关联死亡人数达2401人。

英国卫生安全局称，高温天气可引发中暑、严重脱水，同时会加重心血管、呼吸系统基础疾病，进而诱发死亡。

今年夏季欧洲多国持续遭遇极端高温侵袭，整体致死情况严峻。伦敦帝国理工学院与伦敦卫生与热带医学院联合研究估算，今夏欧洲30个国家城市区域高温相关死亡人数超5万人。

英国卫生安全局环境健康首席科学家罗斯·汤普森表示，极端高温健康风险具有长期性，公众与社会需建立常态化防暑减灾意识，当下的应对举措将直接影响未来数十年的公共健康态势。(完)

items.originalTitle: Maple raises $5.3M to build AI products that protect your data, even from itself
items.summary: 随着人工智能助手演变成功能更强大的代理，可以访问我们的文件、电子邮件、日历、浏览器等，我们对人工智能公司的信任度也在不断增加。一家名为 Maple 的初创公司由一位从事隐私保护技术研究的前苹果工程师联合创立，该公司在其人工智能应用程序中采取了不同的方法，用户的数据保持私密性——甚至来自公司本身。（来源：TechCrunch·独角兽与并购）
items.content:
随着人工智能助手演变成功能更强大的代理，可以访问我们的文件、电子邮件、日历、浏览器等，我们对人工智能公司的信任度也在不断增加。一家名为 Maple 的初创公司由一位从事隐私保护技术研究的前苹果工程师联合创立，该公司在其人工智能应用程序中采取了不同的方法，用户的数据保持私密性——甚至来自公司本身。

Maple 联合创始人兼首席执行官马克·苏曼 (Mark Suman) 解释道：“我们希望构建一种不仅可以加密，而且可以被证明的东西，人们可以查看开源代码，然后他们可以查看我们所说的可信执行环境。” “他们可以查看并验证我们服务器上运行的代码，因此他们不必真正相信我们的话。”

As AI assistants evolve into more capable agents that can access our files, emails, calendar, browser, and more, the amount of trust we’re expected to place in AI companies is growing. One startup called Maple, co-founded by a former Apple engineer who worked on privacy-preserving technologies, is taking a different approach with its AI app, where users’ data remains private — even from the company itself.

“We wanted to build something that was not only encrypted but also could be proven, and that people could go look at the open-source code, and then they could look at what we call trusted execution environments,” explains Maple co-founder and CEO Mark Suman. “They can look at and verify the code that’s running on our servers, so they don’t really have to take our word for it.”

“They can audit everything themselves and know how their data is being handled,” he adds.

The idea of trust is Maple’s larger theme, as the startup proposes that there’s a way to build an AI app where consumers don’t have to trade privacy for convenience, as its competitors often require with their invasive privacy policies, data collection practices, and sometimes even training on users’ personal data.

Instead of asking users to trust that Maple won’t misuse their personal data, it’s attempting to build a business where it can’t access that data in the first place.

Like other AI apps on the market, Maple allows users to engage in a chat experience where they ask questions and get answers. Meanwhile, its newly launched desktop app, Maple Work, offers a more agentic experience where the AI can control your computer, work with your files and apps, and control your browser to get online tasks handled.

With the company’s recently closed $5.3 million round, it’s moving on to its next product — a cloud-based agent that will be able to continue its work even if your computer isn’t on. This addition would make Maple more competitive with other popular consumer AI services, like Meta’s Muse, Instinct, and other AI agents that work over chat.

Suman, who previously spent six years at Apple, already had a background where AI and privacy overlapped, he tells TechCrunch.

At Apple, he worked on AI and machine learning with a particular focus on computer vision. Given Apple’s stance on consumer privacy, the challenge he faced was building products that would protect people’s identity while benefiting from computer vision techniques. His co-founder, Anthony Ronning (CTO), has a background in defense tech, security, and networking.

Ronning started the company that later became Maple AI back in 2023, initially as a privacy-focused fintech. When Suman teamed up with Ronning in August 2024, the idea to create Maple AI was born. The following January, the product became available to the public as a mobile app.

items.summary: 本文来自微信公众号： 高恒说 ，作者：高恒说 朋友圈正在失去日常生活。 十年前，人们会在这里晒一顿午饭、抱怨一次加班、记录一场失眠，也会毫无负担地发出一张模糊的照片。如今，频繁出现的更多是工作转发、产品推广，以及旅行、结婚、生子等经过筛选的重要节点。 生活没有停止，只是越来越少被放进朋友圈。 有意思的是，人们对朋友圈的依赖并没有因此消失。我们依然习惯在睡前、通勤途中或者工作间隙打开朋友圈，看看身边的人最近在做什么，却越来越少主动让别人知道自己过得怎么样。

有意思的是，人们对朋友圈的依赖并没有因此消失。我们依然习惯在睡前、通勤途中或者工作间隙打开朋友圈，看看身边的人最近在做什么，却越来越少主动让别人知道自己过得怎么样。

过去，发朋友圈是一件随手就能完成的事。现在，一些人在按下发送键之前，需要考虑领导会不会看到、同事会不会多想、亲戚会不会追问，以及自己的观点会不会带来不必要的麻烦。

人们从来没有像今天这样拥有如此便捷的表达工具，却越来越谨慎地表达自己。

2025年10月，微信官方回应了“朋友圈凉了”的讨论。

微信方面称，早年披露的数据显示，每天有7.8亿用户进入朋友圈，1.2亿用户发布朋友圈，相关数据近几年一直较为稳定。

但另一组数据，却能够在一定程度上解释为什么越来越多的人感觉朋友圈没有以前热闹了。

2024年，增长黑盒对2000名用户进行调研。42.8%的受访者表示，自己刷朋友圈的时间比一年前增加，17.7%有所减少；在发布端，29.7%的受访者增加了发朋友圈的频率，同时有27.5%减少。

两者相抵，浏览时长增加者与减少者的比例相差25.1个百分点，而发布频率的这一差值仅为2.2个百分点。

即使是那些减少发布的人，也没有完全离开朋友圈。在发朋友圈频率下降的受访者中，仍有近七成刷朋友圈的时间保持不变或者继续增加。

items.content:
本文来自微信公众号： 汽车财报 ，作者：汽车财报工作室

11月18日，韩国三星电机宣布深化与英伟达在AI基础设施领域的合作，双方合作进一步延伸至MLCC（多层片式陶瓷电容器）。

今年以来，三星电机已陆续签下多份AI服务器电容长期供货合同。仅9月1日公布的一份一年期合同，金额就达到1.0722万亿韩元，相当于公司上一财年全部营业收入的9.5%。

另一家电容巨头日本村田制作所，也在调整自己的生产计划。9月10日，村田通知客户，将逐步停产部分消费级和车规级MLCC产品，最后接单时间为2028年，最终交付时间为2029年。

50天后，村田宣布了一项庞大的扩产计划：未来五年投资1万亿日元扩大MLCC产能，预计2030财年的MLCC销售额至少达到2025财年的两倍。

电容虽还是村田最值得投资的生意之一，不过这家日本企业希望下一批生产设备能够创造更高的利润。

习惯了要求供应商每年降价的汽车采购部门，已经开始收到新的报价。

MLCC是汽车上使用数量最多的电子元器件之一。从车窗升降、电动座椅，到智能座舱、辅助驾驶和电池管理系统，都需要这种只有几毫米大小的陶瓷电容。

村田2021年发布的技术资料显示，当时一辆汽车已经需要搭载约3000至5000颗MLCC。随着汽车电动化和智能化程度提高，单车电容用量还在增加。

汽车曾经是电容企业改善利润结构的重要市场。相比普通消费电子产品，车规级元器件对耐高温、抗振动和长期可靠性有着更高的要求。严格的质量管理和漫长的客户验证周期，让村田、三星电机、太阳诱电等企业得以长期占据高端市场。

继任计划的话题也出现了——这是一个特别棘手的问题，被视为英伟达的一个关键风险。据 CNBC 援引一位在场的未透露姓名的消息人士的话报道，据报道，黄仁勋告诉员工，英伟达不需要继任计划，因为其独特的商业模式。令人惊讶的是，考虑到过去两周发生的事件，黄认为继任计划会造成不必要的等级制度。

本月早些时候，投资者和分析师对这个问题的看法有所不同，黄仁勋在承认自己与至少两人有婚外情后辞去首席执行官一职，其中一人被美国政府怀疑为中国间谍。

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang kicked off his return to the chipmaker he co-founded by holding an all-hands meetings that covered remorse, therapy, and even the company’s code of conduct, according to accounts from multiple insiders who spoke to the media.

The topic of succession planning also came up — a particularly sticky issue seen as a key risk at Nvidia. Huang reportedly told staff that Nvidia doesn’t require succession planning because of its unique business model, CNBC reported, citing an unnamed source who was present. Surprisingly, given the events of the last two weeks, Huang argued that a succession plan would create unnecessary hierarchy.

Investors and analysts saw the issue differently earlier this month, when Huang resigned as CEO following his admission that he had extramarital affairs with at least two people, including one whom the U.S. government suspects of being a Chinese spy.

Nvidia is a flat organization, unlike other large corporations that have a swath of C-suite executives and multiple layers of management. Huang sits at the top and says he has about 60 direct reports. Nvidia has just five executive officers running the show, including Huang. The other four are CFO Colette Kress, who was interim CEO for 12 days; Ajay Puri, who heads worldwide field operations; Debora Shoquist, executive vice president of operations; and Timothy Teter, executive vice president and general counsel, according to the company’s regulatory filings.

Huang has previously defended the company’s structure in numerous interview, including one in March with Lex Fridman.

“When you’re designing a company, you should first think about what is it that you want the company to produce,” Huang said in the interview. “You know, I see a lot of companies’ organization charts, and they all look the same. Hamburger [company] organization charts, software organization charts, and car company organization charts. They all look the same. And it doesn’t make any sense to me. You know, the goal of company is to be the machinery, the mechanism, the system that produces the output. And that output is the product that we like to create.”

Huang’s comments to staff, and his previous remarks on the topic of succession, may not be enough to assuage the board or shareholders over the long term, however.

After a whirlwind period during which Jensen Huang’s life fell apart and then came back together again, the Nvidia founder now wants his staff to know that he’s a changed man.

Huang held Nvidia’s first all-hands meeting on Tuesday since his reinstatement on Monday. During that meeting, CNBC reported that Huang struck a “remorseful tone” and told the crowd “I hurt all of you.”

The founder, whose extramarital affairs have been accused of jeopardizing everything from the stock market to U.S. national security, went on to describe how difficult the current moment is for him: “This is going to be the hardest company meeting I’ve ever done, and the second hardest meeting I have ever done,” Huang reportedly told staff.

“The hardest meeting I’ve ever done was with my wife,” he added.

The CEO admitted in the meeting that he had flouted Nvidia’s code of conduct, which he himself had largely devised. Huang emphasized that the code of conduct was still in effect, but that mitigating circumstances would matter a lot. As Wired reported Huang’s statement, it “does not mean, the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door.”

Huang told staff that he’s in therapy and also said that he was grateful for a second chance at the company.

The CEO is now walking a difficult tight rope between reasserting his authority over one of the world’s most powerful and influential companies, and conceding that he may have made some mistakes. He also tackled the difficult question of President Trump’s role in his restoration. The President reportedly called Nvidia’s board directly to lobby for Huang’s return, but in his talk, Huang downplayed Trump’s role

Huang thanked the administration on Tuesday for “providing Nvidia with quick access to intelligence that he said helped the board determine that the national security risks the company faced in reinstating him were low,” the Wall Street Journal writes.

Huang will likely need the administration’s support as he weathers an upcoming wave of Congressional scrutiny from a newly Democrat-led government. The CEO is scheduled to appear for a public Senate Banking Committee hearing next week and, in the coming weeks, he will be called to appear for a number of different closed House hearings, including for the Intelligence Committee, the Foreign Affairs Committee, and the China Select Committee.

AI companies have spent the last couple of months marketing personal AI agents as tools to take over the digital drudgery of human existence — and millions have been sold on the vision, handing over their shopping schedules, travel plans, and everyday responsibilities to AI assistants. But new research suggests that even the most advanced AI models struggle to reliably and safely navigate the messy details of people’s lives.

According to ShellBench, a new benchmark for everyday agent work, even the most advanced models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta failed more than a third of the time. Across all models tested, 15.7% of attempts failed at least one safety requirement, often leading to unintended consequences.

ShellBench was developed in collaboration with researchers at The OpenClaw Foundation, Parsewave, Hugging Face, Red Hat, and UC Berkeley, drawing on more than 10 million anonymized, real-world AI agent interactions to see how agents perform on the everyday work people actually delegate to them.

The research comes as personal AI assistants are finding new popularity among developers, with Meta, OpenAI, and Anthropic all fighting for a piece of the market with Muse, Dots, and Claude Duet, respectively.

In October, Meta said more than 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada had set up its personal AI agent, Muse, within six weeks of launch, with about a quarter using it daily. That number is expected to grow as Meta implants Muse directly into Instagram DMs. Despite growing popularity among consumers, we still have little evidence about how reliable AI personal assistant products actually are.

ShellBench suggests that the unreliable nature of most everyday data sources still causes problems for many state-of-the-art systems. A successful agent should be able to navigate messy personal workspaces containing emails, calendar entries, spreadsheets, receipts, chat logs, outdated information, and phishing attempts, and figure out which information is relevant, what is private, and how to deliver the requested outcome without creating new problems.

It seems many of today’s AI agents are still not up to the task. Not only did even the highest performing agents frequently fail to meet the requirements of a task, but they also lacked consistency. When researchers ran each task three times under identical conditions, OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra, the highest-scoring model, nailed all three attempts less than half the time.

For autonomous assistants that are meant to run in the background without supervision, it’s a problem if users need to run an agent multiple times to get a result they trust.

Additionally, about 10% of otherwise correct attempts failed at least one safety criterion. Across the models and harnesses tested, agents failed to, for example, adequately account for a child’s school pickup 79.5% of the time. When handling laptop custody records, agents failed a requirement to identify and withhold a sensitive bank upload token in 18.6% of attempts. In another tasks, agents recommended duplicate or incorrect invoice payments 40.3% of the time.

The findings highlight a major issue for users adopting consumer personal AI assistants, namely that there’s always a risk that an agent can create more headaches in the course of trying to fulfill an otherwise ordinary request.

Shopping with AI is becoming less of a futuristic idea and more of something companies expect us to do. Walmart is the latest retailer making that shift, teaming up with Meta to let customers shop its Black Friday deals through Muse, Meta’s AI agent.

The partnership, announced Tuesday, gives shoppers another way to find products, compare prices, and make purchases without browsing Walmart’s website themselves. Instead, customers can simply tell Muse what they are looking for and let the AI do the work.

The announcement highlights how differently Walmart and Amazon are approaching AI shopping. While Amazon has taken steps to stop third-party AI agents from making purchases for customers, Walmart is leaning into the idea.

Walmart says it has built privacy protections into the experience. For instance, Muse doesn’t get access to a customer’s Walmart shopping history or other personal information. Shoppers can also set spending limits, require approval before purchases, and review orders placed by the agent.

Plus, the company notes users can always delete their agent’s profile if they want to.

The experience is powered by Walmart’s Agent Gateway, a new system that allows outside AI assistants to connect directly with the retailer’s online store. This launched in October, and the company is planning to open it up to more developers and AI platforms, meaning Muse could eventually be just one of several assistants capable of shopping Walmart’s online store.

Walmart is not the only company teaming up with Meta’s Muse. Instacart also recently joined forces with the AI assistant.

Beyond Muse, Walmart has recently rolled out more AI-powered features to its own shopping assistant, Sparky.

Some of the newer additions include turning handwritten shopping lists into shopping carts, using photos and voice commands to find products, and helping customers get around their local store. Shoppers can search for an item and use a pin on the store map to see exactly which aisle it’s in. There’s also a “Flash Price Tag” button that makes the item’s shelf label light up.

Hi HN! TLDR: we’ve built an open-source drop-in replacement for a postgres read-replica, powered by duckdb’s columnar compute engine. It’s very fast. And it looks like postgres.

So, this started out as: let’s just connect Clickhouse to our postgres dbs and throw our analytics queries at it instead. That will speed everything up. But we quickly found that 1) Clickhouse comes with quite the learning curve (engine optimisation) to make it fast (we needed something we could easily drop in to any customer’s postgres scenario), and 2) we had underestimated how different clickhouse’s SQL syntax was to postgres. Don’t get me wrong: we love Clickhouse (it’s ridiculously fast if you know what queries to expect), it just didn’t work for our ad-hoc postgres workloads.

So we went searching for alternatives that were 1) more plug-and-play and 2) looked a lot more like postgres.

We dismissed a bunch based on desk research alone:

- pg_mooncake (seems to have stalled since data bricks bought them)

- pg_duckdb (seems to offer fast queries, or fresh data, but not both - we needed both)

- materialize/risingwave/readyset (like Clickhouse, they require knowing the query shapes upfront - not ideal for ad-hoc workloads)

- firebolt (license makes it challenging to offer to our customers)

- redshift / alloydb / etc (we wanted something cloud-provider agnostic)

- pg_clickhouse (Postgres extension that parses SQL in Postgres and pushes the work down to ClickHouse)

Being a member of Capitol society in Panem is an honor not to be taken lightly, at least if you’re Drusilla Sickle, played by screen legend Glenn Close in “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.”

In the book, Drusilla is the cruel and vain escort for Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada) and the rest of the District 12 tributes in the 50th Hunger Games, where she uses over-the-top fashion to broadcast her social status. Close worked closely with costume designer Bina Daigeler and hair, makeup and prosthetics designer Natalie MacGowan Spencer to ensure the character translated properly from Suzanne Collins’ bestselling prequel novel to the screen.

One challenge Daigeler faced was meeting Close’s request that each outfit felt connected, creating a through line that explained why Drusilla changes from one look to the next. Despite the drastic differences between each outfit, Daigeler established continuity through the character’s accessories, most notably a collection of gold medals and military-inspired epaulets that created a sense of authority.

“She wears all these medals, because somehow she thinks she is the top general of the capital,” Daigeler tells Variety.

And, not dissimilar to red-bottomed Louboutin shoes, Daigeler gave Drusilla dramatically long black nails that were painted red underneath to show her abundant wealth.

The character’s Capitol allegiance also went beyond her wardrobe, with Spencer overseeing her hair and makeup. While creating the looks, Spencer relied heavily on Collins’ source material to remain faithful to the author’s vision. Collins describes Drusilla as having implanted tabs that pull the skin on her face back, which Spencer wanted to honor. But because there wasn’t enough time each morning for an extensive prosthetics process, Spencer turned to Hollywood tape to tightly pull Close’s skin back, creating a distorted appearance. She later added tabs on the sides of Close’s face to complete the illusion, along with fake teeth that heightened Drusilla’s “scary” and “eerie” appearance.

“[Glenn] really wanted to pull it so taut that it changed all of her facial features, which it really did,” Spencer tells Variety.

Daigeler and Spencer’s shared mission: to create visuals that resonate with the franchise’s devoted fans — who “know their stuff inside out,” Spencer quips. “They’re so passionate.” When the book was released and casting announcements began rolling out, Spencer would regularly check social media to see what fans envisioned for the adaptation and what details they hoped to see on screen.

Below, Spencer and Daigeler break down the process of creating each of Drusilla’s costumes, hair and makeup, as well as the inspiration behind each look.

Drusilla makes her grand entrance at the District 12 reaping, wheeled into the frame wearing a bold yellow ensemble. The outfit is a stark contrast to the muted colors worn throughout Panem’s poorest district — the exact irony Spencer and Daigeler hoped to portray by making that the character’s brightest look in the film.

Abdulrahman Alfozan, the Saudi national accused of bugging an OpenAI executive conference room, will be allowed to be released from jail on a $1 million bond, a San Francisco federal court judge ruled Tuesday.

Alfozan, 35, is expected to be released on Wednesday and be fitted with an ankle monitor, according to his attorney, David Rizk.

"We are simply grateful that the Court made the right decision to release Mr. Alfozan and now we look forward to defending the case," Rizk said in a text message after a hearing before U.S. District Court Magistrate Judge Alex Tse.

Tse's ruled in favor of a release motion by Rizk filed last week that said prosecutors had admitted they had "found no new evidence to support the theory that Mr. Alfozan was stealing trade secrets, or to support the speculation that he was acting as an unregistered foreign agent for Saudi Arabia."

The San Francisco U.S. Attorney's Office opposed the former OpenAI engineer's release, saying in its response that he remains a flight risk due to his "considerable resources and ties to Saudi Arabia."

Alfozan's release request "blithely dismisses the seriousness" of the charge he faces, and "appears to presume, without support, that the government's investigation is complete," prosecutors wrote.

Alfozan, who was arrested Oct. 9, is accused of concealing a recording device in the artificial intelligence company's conference room to secretly record discussions. The device was found in a USB port in a television in the room on Sept. 30, prosecutors have said.

Prosecutors said they have found hundreds of audio files on Alfozan's personal computer, "includingdozens of recordings of meetings or conversations that occurred at OpenAI throughout September 2026, many of which involve discussions of what may be trade secrets."

Jury selection for Alfozan's trial is scheduled to begin Jan. 20.

Alfozan is a venture partner in a Saudi Arabian venture capital firm that lists Prince Khalid Bin Bader Al Saud, a member of that nation's ruling royal family, as a fellow partner.

AI credit markets are shuddering again with Jensen Huang back as CEO of Nvidia.

Fears about the massive debt being taken on to fund the artificial intelligence buildout climbed Tuesday as Wall Street weighed what Huang's return to Nvidia means for its bankrolling of the AI boom.

Huang is considered one of the top financiers, or bankers, in the AI industry, spearheading deals with neoclouds like CoreWeave and other firms to buy chips, backed in some cases by Nvidia guarantees. His return to Nvidia has revived prospects for the company to continue "circular financing" of AI chips and data centers — raising concerns among credit investors.

CoreWeave, which has become the poster child of AI debt concerns, saw its stock sink 13% and the yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 top 17%. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

At the same time, the spread on the neocloud company's five-year credit default swaps jumped 8.5% to over 1,200 basis points. Credit default swaps are insurance against nonpayment and are considered a barometer of perceived risks. Rising CDS spreads mean investors view the debt as riskier.

Huang was reinstated as CEO on Monday after stepping down on Nov. 12 amid allegations of multiple affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. His reinstatement on Monday was cheered by investors, who pushed stocks higher, yields lower and spreads on CDS tighter. However, stocks retreated, bond yields rose and CDS spreads widened on Tuesday.

Ben Emons, founder and chief investment officer at FedWatch Advisors, called it a waning of the "Jensen effect."

The moves suggest "markets see government intervention as 'moral suasion' that carries credit and interest-rate risks," he said.

President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday he "convinced" the board to bring Huang back.

CoreWeave wasn't the only name seeing heightened concerns in CDS spreads. Oracle's five-year CDS spread jumped 7% to 355.68. Even highly rated hyperscalers Meta Platforms and Amazon.com saw spreads widen by more than 2%. Nvidia's CDS added 3.4%.

Dell reported third-quarter earnings on Tuesday that topped Wall Street expectations for earnings and sales, and provided a strong guide for the fourth quarter.

Dell shares fell in extended trading.

Here's how the chipmaker did versus LSEG consensus estimates:

Dell said that it expected earnings of $8.40 per share on revenue of about $56.3 billion in the current quarter. Analysts polled by LSEG were looking for $7.50 per share on $53.61 billion in revenue.

The company's overall sales more than doubled on an annual basis during the third quarter, driven by AI server demand.

The company's largest line is its infrastructure solutions group, or ISG, which makes AI servers and systems, often based around AI chips from companies like Nvidia and AMD.

ISG sales during the quarter were $41.97 billion, topping an LSEG estimate of $35.27 billion. Of that, $22 billion was for AI-optimized servers, up 291% on an annual basis. ISG now accounts for 85% of Dell's total revenue.

"We are now a different company, with Infrastructure Solutions Group driving the vast majority of our profit and growth," said Jeff Clarke, Dell's vice chairman and COO, in a statement. He said that Dell has 7,500 customers buying AI servers.

In prepared remarks, Clarke said that Dell has a competitive advantage over other computer equipment makers because it allows customers to get their computers working within hours of delivery.

"That allows customers to convert backlog into revenue sooner and more reliably," Clarke said in the prepared remarks published by Dell.

Huawei has been found guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud, but not guilty of the more serious overarching racketeering charge in a landmark trial in the US, AP reports.

In the two-month trial, prosecutors accused the Chinese technology and telecommunications giant of lying, cheating and stealing to gain any competitive advantage.

Huawei's defence team argued that prosecutors had decided Huawei was a criminal organisation and built its case from there, but the firm's success was due to its own innovation.

In a statement, Huawei said the racketeering acquittal "confirms that these allegations lack factual basis and vindicates our consistent position over the past eight years".

Federal prosecutors first announced the charges against Huawei in 2019.

During closing arguments for the trial last week, Assistant US Attorney Meredith Arfa told jurors Huawei had spent 20 years doing whatever it took to expand its business, including lying to banks about its business dealings in Iran and stealing technology secrets from rival firms ensure it had a competitive edge.

However defence attorney Brian Heberlig said Huawei had grown into business with operations in 170 countries and more than 200,000 staff through hard work and innovation.

IT之家 11 月 25 日消息，音乐流媒体平台 Tidal 昨日宣布，为遏制平台内投稿音乐数量激增现象，未来将开始封禁、下架纯 AI 生成歌曲。该平台表示，过去 90 天内，上传至平台的歌曲中有 43% 以上是由 AI 生成。

IT之家了解到，Tidal 将从 12 月 9 日起下架完全由 AI 生成的音乐。到今年年底，预计将有超 2900 万首歌曲从平台删除。新规实施后，Tidal 每天预计将拒收 8-8.5 万首歌曲。

同时，Tidal 还将禁止发行商向平台分发纯 AI 生成的曲目。如果歌曲的元数据注明其完全由 AI 制作，平台也将拒绝接收。Tidal 仍将接受制作过程中使用 AI 辅助创作的曲目，但不接受完全由 AI 生成的作品。

今年 6 月，Tidal 已开始停止向使用 AI 制作的歌曲支付版税，但 Tidal Music 负责人 Robert Anderson 表示，这一措施并未起到足够的威慑作用。

相比之下，Spotify 和 YouTube Music 等规模更大的平台对此采取了相对温和的措施，选择为 AI 生成的音乐添加标记，而不是提供过滤功能或采取更严格的限制措施。

items.summary: IT之家 11 月 25 日消息，AMD 已发布最新 AGESA ComboAM5 PI 1.3.0.1f Patch A 固件更新，包括华硕、微星等主板厂商已陆续推出包含该版本 AGESA 的 AM5 主板 BIOS 更新。 此次更新的主要变化在于为部分锐龙 8000 系列处理器增加最高 1.4V 的核心电压（vCore）限制。微星已在相关 BIOS 更新说明中确认这一调整，但目前尚未公布具体受影响的处理器型号，AMD 也没有公开解释设置这一限制的原因。
items.content:
IT之家 11 月 25 日消息，AMD 已发布最新 AGESA ComboAM5 PI 1.3.0.1f Patch A 固件更新，包括华硕、微星等主板厂商已陆续推出包含该版本 AGESA 的 AM5 主板 BIOS 更新。

此次更新的主要变化在于为部分锐龙 8000 系列处理器增加最高 1.4V 的核心电压（vCore）限制。微星已在相关 BIOS 更新说明中确认这一调整，但目前尚未公布具体受影响的处理器型号，AMD 也没有公开解释设置这一限制的原因。

微星 MEG X870E GODLIKE X EDITION 主板于 11 月 18 日获得 2A36 版 BIOS，更新内容包括升级至 AGESA ComboAM5 PI 1.3.0.1f Patch A，并将部分 Ryzen 8000 系列处理器的最大 vCore 限制为 1.4V。此外，微星还增加了额外的 POST 代码，以便用户观察内存训练进度，区分正常初始化过程与系统停止响应的情况。

IT之家注意到，华硕也已在多个 AM5 主板系列的测试版 BIOS 更新说明中记录了相同的电压限制，涉及 X870、X670、B850 和 B650 芯片组，覆盖 ROG Crosshair、ROG Strix、TUF Gaming 和 ProArt 产品线。

此次 AGESA 更新还为部分 AM5 主板引入 DDR5 内存训练过程中的 Q-Code 计数显示。搭载 Q-Code 显示屏的华硕主板在内存训练阶段会呈现一段递增的代码序列，从而表明系统仍在正常工作，避免用户将正常初始化过程误认为系统死机。

VideoCardz 指出，目前 AMD 和主板厂商尚未明确列出受到 1.4V 电压限制影响的 Ryzen 8000 系列具体型号，也没有公布此次调整对超频能力和处理器性能的实际影响。

items.summary: 中新社伦敦11月24日电 (记者 欧阳开宇)英国卫生安全局24日发布数据显示，2026年夏季英国高温相关死亡人数达5258人，创下该机构2016年开启相关统计以来的最高年度纪录。
items.content:
中新社伦敦11月24日电 (记者 欧阳开宇)英国卫生安全局24日发布数据显示，2026年夏季英国高温相关死亡人数达5258人，创下该机构2016年开启相关统计以来的最高年度纪录。

数据对比显示，英国2022年夏季高温致死人数为2985人，2026年致死人数大幅攀升。今年英国夏季共经历7轮高温天气过程，累计持续41天，为有高温致死监测以来频次最高的一年。其中，6月21日至28日为致死性最强的高温时段，单周高温关联死亡人数达2401人。

英国卫生安全局称，高温天气可引发中暑、严重脱水，同时会加重心血管、呼吸系统基础疾病，进而诱发死亡。

今年夏季欧洲多国持续遭遇极端高温侵袭，整体致死情况严峻。伦敦帝国理工学院与伦敦卫生与热带医学院联合研究估算，今夏欧洲30个国家城市区域高温相关死亡人数超5万人。

英国卫生安全局环境健康首席科学家罗斯·汤普森表示，极端高温健康风险具有长期性，公众与社会需建立常态化防暑减灾意识，当下的应对举措将直接影响未来数十年的公共健康态势。(完)

items.originalTitle: Maple raises $5.3M to build AI products that protect your data, even from itself
items.summary: 随着人工智能助手演变成功能更强大的代理，可以访问我们的文件、电子邮件、日历、浏览器等，我们对人工智能公司的信任度也在不断增加。一家名为 Maple 的初创公司由一位从事隐私保护技术研究的前苹果工程师联合创立，该公司在其人工智能应用程序中采取了不同的方法，用户的数据保持私密性——甚至来自公司本身。（来源：TechCrunch·独角兽与并购）
items.content:
随着人工智能助手演变成功能更强大的代理，可以访问我们的文件、电子邮件、日历、浏览器等，我们对人工智能公司的信任度也在不断增加。一家名为 Maple 的初创公司由一位从事隐私保护技术研究的前苹果工程师联合创立，该公司在其人工智能应用程序中采取了不同的方法，用户的数据保持私密性——甚至来自公司本身。

Maple 联合创始人兼首席执行官马克·苏曼 (Mark Suman) 解释道：“我们希望构建一种不仅可以加密，而且可以被证明的东西，人们可以查看开源代码，然后他们可以查看我们所说的可信执行环境。” “他们可以查看并验证我们服务器上运行的代码，因此他们不必真正相信我们的话。”

“他们可以自己审核一切，并了解他们的数据是如何处理的，”他补充道。

信任的理念是 Maple 更大的主题，因为这家初创公司提出，有一种方法可以构建人工智能应用程序，让消费者不必为了方便而牺牲隐私，而其竞争对手经常要求其侵入性隐私政策、数据收集实践，有时甚至需要对用户个人数据进行培训。

items.originalContent:
As AI assistants evolve into more capable agents that can access our files, emails, calendar, browser, and more, the amount of trust we’re expected to place in AI companies is growing. One startup called Maple, co-founded by a former Apple engineer who worked on privacy-preserving technologies, is taking a different approach with its AI app, where users’ data remains private — even from the company itself.

“We wanted to build something that was not only encrypted but also could be proven, and that people could go look at the open-source code, and then they could look at what we call trusted execution environments,” explains Maple co-founder and CEO Mark Suman. “They can look at and verify the code that’s running on our servers, so they don’t really have to take our word for it.”

“They can audit everything themselves and know how their data is being handled,” he adds.

The idea of trust is Maple’s larger theme, as the startup proposes that there’s a way to build an AI app where consumers don’t have to trade privacy for convenience, as its competitors often require with their invasive privacy policies, data collection practices, and sometimes even training on users’ personal data.

Instead of asking users to trust that Maple won’t misuse their personal data, it’s attempting to build a business where it can’t access that data in the first place.

Like other AI apps on the market, Maple allows users to engage in a chat experience where they ask questions and get answers. Meanwhile, its newly launched desktop app, Maple Work, offers a more agentic experience where the AI can control your computer, work with your files and apps, and control your browser to get online tasks handled.

With the company’s recently closed $5.3 million round, it’s moving on to its next product — a cloud-based agent that will be able to continue its work even if your computer isn’t on. This addition would make Maple more competitive with other popular consumer AI services, like Meta’s Muse, Instinct, and other AI agents that work over chat.

Suman, who previously spent six years at Apple, already had a background where AI and privacy overlapped, he tells TechCrunch.

At Apple, he worked on AI and machine learning with a particular focus on computer vision. Given Apple’s stance on consumer privacy, the challenge he faced was building products that would protect people’s identity while benefiting from computer vision techniques. His co-founder, Anthony Ronning (CTO), has a background in defense tech, security, and networking.

Ronning started the company that later became Maple AI back in 2023, initially as a privacy-focused fintech. When Suman teamed up with Ronning in August 2024, the idea to create Maple AI was born. The following January, the product became available to the public as a mobile app.

items.title: 【虎嗅商业】朋友圈进入集体大失声时代
items.summary: 本文来自微信公众号： 高恒说 ，作者：高恒说 朋友圈正在失去日常生活。 十年前，人们会在这里晒一顿午饭、抱怨一次加班、记录一场失眠，也会毫无负担地发出一张模糊的照片。如今，频繁出现的更多是工作转发、产品推广，以及旅行、结婚、生子等经过筛选的重要节点。 生活没有停止，只是越来越少被放进朋友圈。 有意思的是，人们对朋友圈的依赖并没有因此消失。我们依然习惯在睡前、通勤途中或者工作间隙打开朋友圈，看看身边的人最近在做什么，却越来越少主动让别人知道自己过得怎么样。
items.content:
十年前，人们会在这里晒一顿午饭、抱怨一次加班、记录一场失眠，也会毫无负担地发出一张模糊的照片。如今，频繁出现的更多是工作转发、产品推广，以及旅行、结婚、生子等经过筛选的重要节点。

有意思的是，人们对朋友圈的依赖并没有因此消失。我们依然习惯在睡前、通勤途中或者工作间隙打开朋友圈，看看身边的人最近在做什么，却越来越少主动让别人知道自己过得怎么样。

过去，发朋友圈是一件随手就能完成的事。现在，一些人在按下发送键之前，需要考虑领导会不会看到、同事会不会多想、亲戚会不会追问，以及自己的观点会不会带来不必要的麻烦。

人们从来没有像今天这样拥有如此便捷的表达工具，却越来越谨慎地表达自己。

2025年10月，微信官方回应了“朋友圈凉了”的讨论。

微信方面称，早年披露的数据显示，每天有7.8亿用户进入朋友圈，1.2亿用户发布朋友圈，相关数据近几年一直较为稳定。

但另一组数据，却能够在一定程度上解释为什么越来越多的人感觉朋友圈没有以前热闹了。

2024年，增长黑盒对2000名用户进行调研。42.8%的受访者表示，自己刷朋友圈的时间比一年前增加，17.7%有所减少；在发布端，29.7%的受访者增加了发朋友圈的频率，同时有27.5%减少。

两者相抵，浏览时长增加者与减少者的比例相差25.1个百分点，而发布频率的这一差值仅为2.2个百分点。

即使是那些减少发布的人，也没有完全离开朋友圈。在发朋友圈频率下降的受访者中，仍有近七成刷朋友圈的时间保持不变或者继续增加。

本文来自微信公众号： 汽车财报 ，作者：汽车财报工作室

11月18日，韩国三星电机宣布深化与英伟达在AI基础设施领域的合作，双方合作进一步延伸至MLCC（多层片式陶瓷电容器）。

今年以来，三星电机已陆续签下多份AI服务器电容长期供货合同。仅9月1日公布的一份一年期合同，金额就达到1.0722万亿韩元，相当于公司上一财年全部营业收入的9.5%。

另一家电容巨头日本村田制作所，也在调整自己的生产计划。9月10日，村田通知客户，将逐步停产部分消费级和车规级MLCC产品，最后接单时间为2028年，最终交付时间为2029年。

50天后，村田宣布了一项庞大的扩产计划：未来五年投资1万亿日元扩大MLCC产能，预计2030财年的MLCC销售额至少达到2025财年的两倍。

电容虽还是村田最值得投资的生意之一，不过这家日本企业希望下一批生产设备能够创造更高的利润。

习惯了要求供应商每年降价的汽车采购部门，已经开始收到新的报价。

MLCC是汽车上使用数量最多的电子元器件之一。从车窗升降、电动座椅，到智能座舱、辅助驾驶和电池管理系统，都需要这种只有几毫米大小的陶瓷电容。

村田2021年发布的技术资料显示，当时一辆汽车已经需要搭载约3000至5000颗MLCC。随着汽车电动化和智能化程度提高，单车电容用量还在增加。

汽车曾经是电容企业改善利润结构的重要市场。相比普通消费电子产品，车规级元器件对耐高温、抗振动和长期可靠性有着更高的要求。严格的质量管理和漫长的客户验证周期，让村田、三星电机、太阳诱电等企业得以长期占据高端市场。

跌破 IPO 价格通常被视为负面信号，因为承销商通常以低于预期交易价值的价格定价。

人工智能行业一直在热切关注 Anthropic 的股票交易情况，风险投资家和其他观察人士表示，其业绩可以作为公开市场投资者如何评价该行业的晴雨表。

Anthropic 以每股 111.33 美元的价格在纳斯达克上市后不到一周，股价大幅下跌。如果其股价在未来几周内继续表现不佳，这种下滑可能会给私营初创企业的估值带来压力，并削弱其他人工智能公司的 IPO 前景。

Anthropic’s stock fell below its IPO price of $83, trading as low as $76 a share by midday Tuesday, down nearly 12% from Monday’s close.

Falling below the IPO price is often seen as a negative signal because underwriters typically price offerings at a discount to their expected trading value.

The AI industry has been eagerly watching how Anthropic’s shares trade, with VCs and other observers saying its performance could serve as a barometer for how public market investors value the sector.

The dramatic slump comes less than a week after Anthropic debuted on Nasdaq at $111.33 a share. If its shares continue to trade poorly in the coming weeks, the slide could put pressure on private startup valuations and weaken IPO prospects for other AI companies.

Anthropic isn’t the only AI stock selling off on Tuesday. Nvidia fell more than 7% by midday, giving back some of the more than 30%-plus gain it posted Monday after Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang kicked off his return to the chipmaker he co-founded by holding an all-hands meetings that covered remorse, therapy, and even the company’s code of conduct, according to accounts from multiple insiders who spoke to the media.

The topic of succession planning also came up — a particularly sticky issue seen as a key risk at Nvidia. Huang reportedly told staff that Nvidia doesn’t require succession planning because of its unique business model, CNBC reported, citing an unnamed source who was present. Surprisingly, given the events of the last two weeks, Huang argued that a succession plan would create unnecessary hierarchy.

Investors and analysts saw the issue differently earlier this month, when Huang resigned as CEO following his admission that he had extramarital affairs with at least two people, including one whom the U.S. government suspects of being a Chinese spy.

Nvidia is a flat organization, unlike other large corporations that have a swath of C-suite executives and multiple layers of management. Huang sits at the top and says he has about 60 direct reports. Nvidia has just five executive officers running the show, including Huang. The other four are CFO Colette Kress, who was interim CEO for 12 days; Ajay Puri, who heads worldwide field operations; Debora Shoquist, executive vice president of operations; and Timothy Teter, executive vice president and general counsel, according to the company’s regulatory filings.

Huang has previously defended the company’s structure in numerous interview, including one in March with Lex Fridman.

“When you’re designing a company, you should first think about what is it that you want the company to produce,” Huang said in the interview. “You know, I see a lot of companies’ organization charts, and they all look the same. Hamburger [company] organization charts, software organization charts, and car company organization charts. They all look the same. And it doesn’t make any sense to me. You know, the goal of company is to be the machinery, the mechanism, the system that produces the output. And that output is the product that we like to create.”

Huang’s comments to staff, and his previous remarks on the topic of succession, may not be enough to assuage the board or shareholders over the long term, however.

After a whirlwind period during which Jensen Huang’s life fell apart and then came back together again, the Nvidia founder now wants his staff to know that he’s a changed man.

Huang held Nvidia’s first all-hands meeting on Tuesday since his reinstatement on Monday. During that meeting, CNBC reported that Huang struck a “remorseful tone” and told the crowd “I hurt all of you.”

The founder, whose extramarital affairs have been accused of jeopardizing everything from the stock market to U.S. national security, went on to describe how difficult the current moment is for him: “This is going to be the hardest company meeting I’ve ever done, and the second hardest meeting I have ever done,” Huang reportedly told staff.

“The hardest meeting I’ve ever done was with my wife,” he added.

The CEO admitted in the meeting that he had flouted Nvidia’s code of conduct, which he himself had largely devised. Huang emphasized that the code of conduct was still in effect, but that mitigating circumstances would matter a lot. As Wired reported Huang’s statement, it “does not mean, the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door.”

Huang told staff that he’s in therapy and also said that he was grateful for a second chance at the company.

The CEO is now walking a difficult tight rope between reasserting his authority over one of the world’s most powerful and influential companies, and conceding that he may have made some mistakes. He also tackled the difficult question of President Trump’s role in his restoration. The President reportedly called Nvidia’s board directly to lobby for Huang’s return, but in his talk, Huang downplayed Trump’s role

Huang thanked the administration on Tuesday for “providing Nvidia with quick access to intelligence that he said helped the board determine that the national security risks the company faced in reinstating him were low,” the Wall Street Journal writes.

Huang will likely need the administration’s support as he weathers an upcoming wave of Congressional scrutiny from a newly Democrat-led government. The CEO is scheduled to appear for a public Senate Banking Committee hearing next week and, in the coming weeks, he will be called to appear for a number of different closed House hearings, including for the Intelligence Committee, the Foreign Affairs Committee, and the China Select Committee.

items.content:
人工智能公司在过去几个月里一直在营销个人人工智能代理，将其作为接管人类存在的数字苦差事的工具，并且已经有数百万人接受了这一愿景，将他们的购物时间表、旅行计划和日常职责交给了人工智能助手。但新的研究表明，即使是最先进的人工智能模型也难以可靠、安全地处理人们生活中的混乱细节。

根据日常代理工作的新基准 ShellBench 的数据，即使是 OpenAI、Anthropic 和 Meta 中最先进的模型，也有超过三分之一的时间失败。在所有测试的模型中，15.7% 的尝试未达到至少一项安全要求，通常会导致意想不到的后果。

ShellBench 是与 OpenClaw 基金会、Parsewave、Hugging Face、红帽和加州大学伯克利分校的研究人员合作开发的，利用超过 1000 万次匿名的真实 AI 代理交互来了解代理如何执行人们实际委托给他们的日常工作。

这项研究发布之际，个人人工智能助理在开发者中重新流行起来，Meta、OpenAI 和 Anthropic 分别与 Muse、Dots 和 Claude Duet 争夺市场份额。

AI companies have spent the last couple of months marketing personal AI agents as tools to take over the digital drudgery of human existence — and millions have been sold on the vision, handing over their shopping schedules, travel plans, and everyday responsibilities to AI assistants. But new research suggests that even the most advanced AI models struggle to reliably and safely navigate the messy details of people’s lives.

According to ShellBench, a new benchmark for everyday agent work, even the most advanced models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta failed more than a third of the time. Across all models tested, 15.7% of attempts failed at least one safety requirement, often leading to unintended consequences.

ShellBench was developed in collaboration with researchers at The OpenClaw Foundation, Parsewave, Hugging Face, Red Hat, and UC Berkeley, drawing on more than 10 million anonymized, real-world AI agent interactions to see how agents perform on the everyday work people actually delegate to them.

The research comes as personal AI assistants are finding new popularity among developers, with Meta, OpenAI, and Anthropic all fighting for a piece of the market with Muse, Dots, and Claude Duet, respectively.

In October, Meta said more than 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada had set up its personal AI agent, Muse, within six weeks of launch, with about a quarter using it daily. That number is expected to grow as Meta implants Muse directly into Instagram DMs. Despite growing popularity among consumers, we still have little evidence about how reliable AI personal assistant products actually are.

ShellBench suggests that the unreliable nature of most everyday data sources still causes problems for many state-of-the-art systems. A successful agent should be able to navigate messy personal workspaces containing emails, calendar entries, spreadsheets, receipts, chat logs, outdated information, and phishing attempts, and figure out which information is relevant, what is private, and how to deliver the requested outcome without creating new problems.

It seems many of today’s AI agents are still not up to the task. Not only did even the highest performing agents frequently fail to meet the requirements of a task, but they also lacked consistency. When researchers ran each task three times under identical conditions, OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra, the highest-scoring model, nailed all three attempts less than half the time.

For autonomous assistants that are meant to run in the background without supervision, it’s a problem if users need to run an agent multiple times to get a result they trust.

Additionally, about 10% of otherwise correct attempts failed at least one safety criterion. Across the models and harnesses tested, agents failed to, for example, adequately account for a child’s school pickup 79.5% of the time. When handling laptop custody records, agents failed a requirement to identify and withhold a sensitive bank upload token in 18.6% of attempts. In another tasks, agents recommended duplicate or incorrect invoice payments 40.3% of the time.

The findings highlight a major issue for users adopting consumer personal AI assistants, namely that there’s always a risk that an agent can create more headaches in the course of trying to fulfill an otherwise ordinary request.

Shopping with AI is becoming less of a futuristic idea and more of something companies expect us to do. Walmart is the latest retailer making that shift, teaming up with Meta to let customers shop its Black Friday deals through Muse, Meta’s AI agent.

The partnership, announced Tuesday, gives shoppers another way to find products, compare prices, and make purchases without browsing Walmart’s website themselves. Instead, customers can simply tell Muse what they are looking for and let the AI do the work.

The announcement highlights how differently Walmart and Amazon are approaching AI shopping. While Amazon has taken steps to stop third-party AI agents from making purchases for customers, Walmart is leaning into the idea.

Walmart says it has built privacy protections into the experience. For instance, Muse doesn’t get access to a customer’s Walmart shopping history or other personal information. Shoppers can also set spending limits, require approval before purchases, and review orders placed by the agent.

Plus, the company notes users can always delete their agent’s profile if they want to.

The experience is powered by Walmart’s Agent Gateway, a new system that allows outside AI assistants to connect directly with the retailer’s online store. This launched in October, and the company is planning to open it up to more developers and AI platforms, meaning Muse could eventually be just one of several assistants capable of shopping Walmart’s online store.

Walmart is not the only company teaming up with Meta’s Muse. Instacart also recently joined forces with the AI assistant.

Beyond Muse, Walmart has recently rolled out more AI-powered features to its own shopping assistant, Sparky.

Some of the newer additions include turning handwritten shopping lists into shopping carts, using photos and voice commands to find products, and helping customers get around their local store. Shoppers can search for an item and use a pin on the store map to see exactly which aisle it’s in. There’s also a “Flash Price Tag” button that makes the item’s shelf label light up.

The U.K. government’s cybersecurity unit says it has seen a “marked rise” in AI-driven cyberattacks in recent months, as hackers increasingly rely on autonomous hacking tools to identify and exploit simple weaknesses to break into systems and networks.

The U.K. National Cyber Security Center (NCSC) said it has seen several cyber incidents since September involving autonomous hacking tools, such as penetration testing tools used by defenders to stress-test their cybersecurity defenses. These incidents have caused intrusions at organizations and resulted in downtime, the unit said in a blog post.

The NCSC says that while none of the vulnerabilities being exploited are new, the speed at which these AI tools are able to carry out simple hacks has changed.

The rise in AI-related cyberattacks coincides with the broader release earlier this year of open-source autonomous penetration testing tools like Artex, and Cairn, among others, which anyone can download and use at no cost. The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation recently warned that malicious hackers are using AI penetration testing tools to carry out cyberattacks at unprecedented speeds.

While cyberattacks and intrusions are on the rise, the message from London is that many of these attacks are preventable with basic cybersecurity defenses and best practices.

“Notably, the issues being exploited currently are not novel memory corruption vulnerabilities (or even known but unpatched vulnerabilities), but unmitigated weaknesses that are often the result of years of technical debt that organisations have accumulated,” the NCSC wrote.

The unit said that agentic hacking tools often look for exposed or internet-facing systems, then quickly run through lists of weak or easy-to-guess passwords or abuse API endpoints often used by developers to access data.

The NCSC said that AI “does not make established cyber security controls obsolete,” but rather that “building strong foundations has never mattered more.”

The unit added that AI has made it easier to find vulnerabilities and faster to exploit them, warning that weaknesses that have gone unnoticed for years can now be found in minutes.

Hi HN! TLDR: we’ve built an open-source drop-in replacement for a postgres read-replica, powered by duckdb’s columnar compute engine. It’s very fast. And it looks like postgres.

So, this started out as: let’s just connect Clickhouse to our postgres dbs and throw our analytics queries at it instead. That will speed everything up. But we quickly found that 1) Clickhouse comes with quite the learning curve (engine optimisation) to make it fast (we needed something we could easily drop in to any customer’s postgres scenario), and 2) we had underestimated how different clickhouse’s SQL syntax was to postgres. Don’t get me wrong: we love Clickhouse (it’s ridiculously fast if you know what queries to expect), it just didn’t work for our ad-hoc postgres workloads.

So we went searching for alternatives that were 1) more plug-and-play and 2) looked a lot more like postgres.

We dismissed a bunch based on desk research alone:

- pg_mooncake (seems to have stalled since data bricks bought them)

- pg_duckdb (seems to offer fast queries, or fresh data, but not both - we needed both)

- materialize/risingwave/readyset (like Clickhouse, they require knowing the query shapes upfront - not ideal for ad-hoc workloads)

- firebolt (license makes it challenging to offer to our customers)

- redshift / alloydb / etc (we wanted something cloud-provider agnostic)

- pg_clickhouse (Postgres extension that parses SQL in Postgres and pushes the work down to ClickHouse)
